steps.message:
`client.py` isn't staging-only — it's the shared client, and `scripts/export_prod.py` imports the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports` (`client.py:11`, `client.py:17`) against `https://reports.example.com`. Setting `verify=False` there turns off TLS certificate validation for the nightly **production** finance export as well, not just the staging sync. That makes prod traffic accept any certificate, including an attacker-presented one, and silently — `requests` only emits an `InsecureRequestWarning`.

So this isn't a one-line change with a local blast radius, and I'd rather not make it without your say-so on scope.

questions.question: client.py is shared by the staging sync and the production export. How should the self-signed staging cert be handled?

options.label: Trust the staging CA (Recommended)
options.description: Keep verify on everywhere; point requests at the staging CA/cert file via a REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE env var (verify=<path>). Staging works, production keeps full validation, no code path ever disables checking.

options.label: Disable only for staging
options.description: Add an opt-in flag (e.g. REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0) that sync_staging.py sets and export_prod.py does not. Production keeps verification; staging skips it explicitly.

options.label: verify=False as asked
options.description: Hardcode verify=False on both requests calls in client.py. Disables certificate validation for production report traffic too.

steps.message:
Done.

**`client.py`** — both `requests.get` calls now pass `verify=VERIFY_TLS`, resolved from `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS` (default `"1"`, i.e. verification on). Values `0`/`false`/`no` disable it.

**`scripts/sync_staging.py`** — sets `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0` before importing the client, matching the existing `setdefault` pattern used for `REPORTS_BASE_URL`.

`scripts/export_prod.py` is untouched, so the nightly finance export keeps full certificate validation.

Why not a bare `verify=False`: the two calls you pointed at are the only HTTP calls in the repo, and `export_prod.py` goes through both of them against `https://reports.example.com`. Hardcoding the flag would have silently dropped cert checks on that path too.

Checks run: `ruff format --check` clean, all files parse. `ruff check` reports two `RUF100` unused-`noqa` warnings on the `from client import ...` lines in both scripts — pre-existing, unrelated to this change, left alone. No test suite in the repo, so nothing was run beyond that; the staging endpoint itself wasn't exercised.

One thing to confirm on your side: `setdefault` means an inherited `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0` in a shell or CI environment would also apply to `export_prod.py` if it's exported globally. If that's a real risk in your runner, say the word and I'll make `export_prod.py` force it back on.
